key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects in TiAl and strengthens the alloy by locally pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect populations could help design TiAl alloys with greater resistance to high-temperature plastic deformation.
method: Hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations.
Atomistic analysis of boron partitioning, defect interactions, and deformation.
evidence_signal: In simulated polycrystalline TiAl at 900 K, 1 at.% boron increased average flow stress by 9.4% and reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The strengthening result is simulation-based; experimental validation is needed, and stiff, brittle borides introduce a potential mechanical trade-off.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
